title: 200万销量、2000万玩家之后，AI游戏找到新方向了？
text:
过去两年，生成式AI在游戏行业引发的争议，大多集中在美术等内容生产环节。相比批量生成素材，用AI创造过去难以实现的玩法，或许更值得关注。
传统游戏擅长模拟规则明确的系统，却很难处理模糊的人类概念。如今，一批中小团队开始把AI直接放进核心循环：敌人会模仿队友的声音和行为，AI主持人能理解玩家自由输入的求生方案，虚拟社交网络中的角色则拥有各自的性格和人际关系。
外媒Naavik最新的一篇报告中，《MIMESIS》《Death by AI》和《Status》分别代表了3种尝试。
它们的市场表现证明，玩家对AI原生玩法存在需求，也暴露了这一方向的共同难题——模型能力尚不稳定，玩法的新鲜感可能快速消退，每一次交互还会产生持续的推理成本。
当AI成为玩法的一部分，团队不仅要考虑游戏是否有趣，还要计算玩家每多玩一局，公司会多花多少钱。产品的技术架构、经济系统和商业化设计，也要围绕这项新增的可变成本重新调整。
以下为罗斯基编译整理的主要内容：
·《MIMESIS》：怪物扮演你的队友
《MIMESIS》（迷魅狩猎）由ReLU Games开发，于2025年10月登陆Steam，以9.99美元的价格开启抢先体验。
ReLU成立于2023年，是KRAFTON旗下专注AI与深度学习的独立工作室。据KRAFTON披露，截至2026年7月，游戏累计销量已经突破200万份，成为ReLU目前最成功的产品。
这是一款支持4人合作的生存恐怖游戏。玩家面对的敌人Mimesis能从行为和声音两个层面模仿真人。
行为方面，AI会根据游戏情境作出反应。团队特意让模型针对同一种情况生成不同选择，例如一个敌人可能发起攻击，另一个则会转身逃跑，以免形成容易识破的固定模式。
游戏会通过麦克风录下玩家在当局说过的话，再选择合适的片段播放。语音内容本身并非AI生成，AI负责结合对话和游戏状态，判断何时、以何种方式使用这些录音，让伪装显得更加可信。
这项机制改变了合作恐怖游戏的常见问题。玩家担心的不再只是怪物在哪里，还要判断眼前的人究竟是不是队友。AI模糊了敌我边界，并迫使玩家自行发展出一套验证身份和行动的方法。类似体验很难依靠传统脚本NPC实现。
不过，核心卖点也成了玩家批评最多的部分。现阶段的AI还不足以始终维持可信的伪装。玩家一旦熟悉系统，可能通过重复语音、行为规律等线索找到稳定的应对方式，依靠不确定性制造的恐惧也会逐渐减弱。
游戏的月活跃用户在上线初期快速增长，2025年12月达到56.2万，此后再未回到这一高点。ReLU也承认，抢先体验版本缺少足够内容，无法支持长期重复游玩。因此，用户流失不能全部归因于AI。
毕竟《MIMESIS》大约在两年前进入开发，而两年对AI技术而言已经相当漫长。它更适合被视为玩家需求的早期信号，无法代表今天乃至未来模型能力的上限。
·《Death by AI》：玩家对抗AI裁判
Little Umbrella Games于2023年12月推出《Death by AI》，目前覆盖Discord、网页和iOS，采用免费下载+内购付费的商业模式。
游戏于2024年5月登陆Discord后迅速走红，前3个月吸引了超过2000万名玩家，也帮助团队在2025年1月完成200万美元种子轮融资。
游戏中玩家会被投入一个致命场景，例如遭遇毒蛇围困，并需要在60秒内写下自己的求生方案。游戏没有预设行动选项，玩家可以输入任何计划。AI游戏主持人会理解这段内容，判断玩家能否活下来，并描述最终结果。
传统游戏通常拥有固定的行动与结果空间，设计者提前规定玩家能做什么，以及每种行为对应什么后果。《Death by AI》把判断权交给模型，大幅扩展了输入和结果的可能性。
这套规则下还藏着另一层玩法。玩家既要解决求生题目，也要研究如何说服甚至欺骗AI，让它认可自己的方案。开发团队将核心循环概括为想办法骗AI放你一条生路。
产品快速走红后，团队很快遇到了AI原生游戏最现实的问题——每玩一局都会产生成本。
游戏最初使用OpenAI生成文本，并通过ElevenLabs处理语音。上线仅3天，暴涨的用户规模就让这套技术组合难以承受。玩家参与度越高，模型调用次数越多，公司的支出也随之增加。
团队没有削减AI交互，而是从成本和收入两端解决问题。
一方面改用更便宜的模型路由与推理基础设施，并与Inworld合作降低单用户成本；另一方面加入订阅、内购和额外内容包。高峰期，《Death by AI》每天会生成约12亿个文本Token和3500万个语音字符。
对这类产品来说，模型推理已经成为直接营业成本，技术选型对商业模型的影响不亚于玩法和付费设计。未来，团队可以有选择地调用模型，将部分推理转移到玩家设备，或采用本地与云端结合的架构。
随着推理价格继续下降，AI原生游戏的成本结构也可能得到显著改善。
·《Status》：在AI社交网络里经营另一种人生
WishRoll开发的《Status》于2025年2月正式上线，覆盖iOS和Android，商业化模式包括内购、订阅与广告变现。WishRoll在种子轮和A轮共融资1700万美元，相关消息于2026年5月公布。
团队将游戏形容为社交媒体版《模拟人生》。玩家可以创建一套虚拟身份，在类似社交平台的信息流中发帖、回复和发送私信。与玩家互动的其他用户全部由AI驱动，并拥有各自的性格、关系和记忆。
这个概念很快获得市场反馈。
Sensor Tower数据显示，游戏上线次月的月活跃用户达到约270万。此后活跃度持续回落，直到2026年才重新增长，2026年7月恢复至约160万。
规模化成本同样是《Status》早期面对的主要问题。限量测试期间，原有AI架构据称每天每名用户需要花费12—15美元，团队不得不在全面上线前重新设计基础设施。
通过与Inworld合作，WishRoll表示AI成本最终降低了95%以上，在支持超过50万日活用户的同时，将日均游戏时长维持在1.5小时以上。成本下降还让团队有能力加入实时活动等此前难以负担的功能。
随后，《Status》为AI社交体验加入了常见的手游经济系统。玩家行动需要消耗能量，可以通过内购、订阅和激励广告补充。这些调整推动ARPDAU显著提高，也引发了用户不满。
2025年11月开始的商业化重构，让产品从相对慷慨的免费应用逐渐转向以订阅为主。商店评论中的付费相关抱怨在当年12月达到高峰，2026年针对广告的投诉也明显增多。
同期，游戏的次留与7留均有所下降。
不过，这一阶段正好赶上团队加大付费买量，新增用户结构发生变化，因此不能把留存下滑全部归咎于商业化。可以确定的是，《Status》正在从依赖自然增长转向更积极的买量获客。
这说明，提高商业化强度确实能改善ARPDAU，也可能损害玩家感受。当AI推理深入核心玩法后，团队需要根据技术成本反复调整经济系统，这种变化很容易传导至留存和口碑。
·AI原生游戏还在非常早期
这3款产品都存在明显短板，也展示了AI在玩法层面的价值。《MIMESIS》让敌人能够理解情境并伪装成队友；《Death by AI》允许玩家自由提出方案，再由模型解释结果；《Status》则模拟了一套持续运转的社会关系。
AI让玩家关系变成了可交互的游戏机制，这比低成本生产更多美术与文本更有想象空间。
现阶段仍有3个问题需要解决：
首先，模型能力不足可能限制长期体验。一两年前开发的产品很快会显得落后，今天的案例不能代表未来上限。
其次，AI并非免费的内容来源。推理价格虽然持续下降，部分计算也可以迁移到用户设备，但每次交互产生的可变成本仍会影响经济系统和商业模式。
最后，这些尝试几乎都来自中小团队。即使ReLU背靠KRAFTON，也只是集团内部相对独立的工作室。
《MIMESIS》《Death by AI》和《Status》都谈不上改写市场的超级爆款，却已经证明玩家愿意尝试AI驱动的新玩法。随着模型和开发方法继续成熟，率先探索这些方向的很可能仍是小型团队。
AI原生游戏的浪潮尚未真正到来，目前看到的只是最早一批涟漪。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: 从Demo卷到工作台，AI游戏进入下半场
text:
过去半年，罗斯基陆续看过不少AI游戏比赛。
大部分时候，选手要回答的问题都很直接：能不能用AI做出一款游戏？美术、代码和玩法分别由AI完成了多少？最终的Demo是否能够正常运行？
9月13日举行的腾讯云黑客松全球总决赛，却临时给16支游戏赛道队伍出了一道更难的题。此前初赛比的是能不能借助AI把游戏做出来，总决赛则进一步追问——做完这款游戏后，基于 WorkBuddy、Miora、CodeBuddy 等Agent工具平台，你留下了什么？
参赛者需要回过头拆解整个开发过程，并决定哪些经验能够被保留下来，哪些重复劳动可以交给AI，又该如何把这些能力变成其他创作者也能使用的工作台。
这个命题也让罗斯基对比赛产生了兴趣。
2026腾讯云黑客松以AI CAN DO IT为主题，历时150天，覆盖华南、华北、华东、港澳和东南亚五大赛区，吸引一万多名选手参加，共收到上千份作品。最终有42支团队入选决赛（游戏、智能体、动画三大赛道）。而罗斯基从华北赛区一路跟到全球总决赛，并受邀担任游戏赛道评委。
几个月前，不少参赛作品还停留在验证创意的Demo阶段。等到深圳总决赛再见到这些团队时，一些项目已经发生了很大变化。
9月13日上午，在腾讯总部企鹅岛腾云中心，16支游戏队伍依次登台。有人展示覆盖地图与Agent NPC的3D游戏生产平台，有人把游戏开发中的任务管理和人工验收做成了一套工作流，还有人把原本用于游戏的能力迁移到了教学、文旅、公益。
一上午看下来，罗斯基非常感慨。
这群年轻创作者开始尝试把自己的开发经验封装起来，把一次性的作品变成能够反复使用的生产能力。AI游戏竞赛比拼的重点，也开始转向谁能找到真实需求，组织复杂流程，并让一个偶然跑通的项目持续运行下去。
从做游戏，到把方法留给后来者
《记得回家》团队的变化很有代表性。
这款作品以阿尔茨海默症为主题。初赛阶段，团队主要精力还放在游戏本身。到了总决赛，他们拿出了一套3D游戏创作平台，希望将开发《记得回家》时遇到的问题集中解决。
平台会先帮助创作者梳理剧情，并通过长期记忆维持前后设定的一致。剧情确定后，AI会继续推导场景需要多少房间，人物应该如何移动，关键道具该放在哪里。地图先以满足玩法为目标搭出框架，随后再完善外观。
3D场景也是AI最容易失控的环节之一。为了减少创作者反复修改提示词的麻烦，团队给Blender和Godot制作了插件。用户可以直接在编辑器中选中某件物体，然后像给设计稿写批注一样提出修改意见。
平台还会尝试记住自己犯过的错误。
在制作一款游戏时，AI曾把场景里的玻璃全部做成不透明材质。团队纠正问题后，系统会分析这次修改是否具有通用价值。如果答案是肯定的，这条经验便会进入后续流程。下一次遇到相似场景时，AI可以提前避开同样的问题。
这种能力来自团队真实的开发经历。他们先把一款游戏做出来，再回头翻看与AI的聊天记录，从中找到反复出现的障碍。工作台由此成为游戏开发过程的副产品，也比凭空设计一套工具更贴近实际需求。
四川美术学院的团队也在解决类似的问题，只是他们把注意力放在了3D开发的门槛上。
团队成员大多没有完整的游戏开发经验。在制作初赛作品的过程中，他们发现自己花费大量时间让AI理解需求。用户说想做一款游戏，对AI来说远远不够。它必须继续确认游戏类型，理解核心体验，再逐步收紧方向。
基于这些经历，团队制作了Easy3D。工作台不会在收到一句需求后立刻开始生成，而是先陪用户聊想法。随着选项逐步确定，模糊的创意才会变成能够执行的开发方案。
团队还发现，单纯依赖一份文字说明，很难保证不同模型稳定复现某种能力。相比抽象的规则，完整案例往往更容易被AI理解。于是，他们把经过测试的开发方法整理成典型实践，允许其他用户直接调用，也可以在原有基础上继续改进。
AI可以迅速交付，最终验收仍然属于人
《中华食肆》团队注意到的，是AI开发中的另一个麻烦。
AI经常告诉用户某项任务已经完成，但开发者很难立刻确认结果。完全相信AI可能留下隐患。每次从头检查，又会抵消自动化带来的效率。
为此，团队把开发流程做成了一块任务看板。AI可以理解需求并执行任务，也能主动汇报进度，但它最多只能把任务推进到待检查。只有经过用户确认，任务才会进入完成状态。
工作台还会记录每次修改，并自动整理项目结构。这样一来，即便中途换人接手，新成员也能快速理解此前发生了什么。过去犯过的错误不会被漫长的对话淹没，相同功能也不必重复实现。
团队把这套原则概括为一句话：判断留给人，执行交给AI。
在创意工作台中，他们又把《中华食肆》的内容带进了现实生活。
用户可以拍下冰箱里的食材，或者直接通过语音完成录入。工作台会根据现有库存推荐菜品，并将烹饪过程拆解成容易执行的步骤。做完之后，用户还能上传照片，保存关于这顿饭的记忆。
游戏里的百味图由此在现实中延续。玩家在游戏里收集中国菜，也在生活中积累自己的食忆。团队没有刻意给原作增加一层复杂玩法，而是找到了一个与游戏主题自然相连的使用场景。
除此之外，来自中关村学院与上海交通大学等学校的“AI＋游戏”方向博士生团队，共同开发了《城市荣耀·KPL传奇之路》，融合电竞策略经营与城市文旅，让玩家在战队经营和赛事对抗中探索地域文化。
《岐黄异邦录》则将游戏提炼为“交互叙事的载体”，将整套方法论打造为了综合性的工作台，使作品拓展至更广群体、更多领域，以期让每个人都能用游戏的方式表达自我。
《大唐风华录》团队成员仅一人，今年开始通过WorkBuddy接触到了Vibe Coding。选手一人通过WorkBuddy制作了策划案，并利用产品集成的 Skills、MCP 与专家生态，一周时间内做出了1000张美术图与所有的游戏配乐，并同步上架了qq音乐专辑，完成了完整的开发。在过去，这至少需要一个团队立项2个月以上才能完成。
此外还有很多团队也给出了非常精彩的路演内容，篇幅所限在此不一一列举。
做出Demo之后，困难才真正开始
聆听路演时罗斯基注意到，现场出现了不少令人印象深刻的效率数字。
有选手用48小时完成一款游戏。也有团队展示了一款只用8小时制作的FPS Demo。
来自马来西亚理工大学的选手独自参赛，为沟通训练游戏设计了大量NPC与练习场景。
演示结束时，她用中文说道：AI都能做到，我也能做到。我只是一个人，所以你们还在等什么？
这样的案例很容易让人觉得，游戏开发正在迅速变成一件简单的事。但在现场交流中，选手反复提到一个共同判断：AI已经很擅长把创意变成原型，从原型走向稳定产品依然需要大量人工投入。
AI可以快速写出一个玩法，却无法可靠判断它是否真的好玩。它能批量生成美术资源，也很难独立维持统一的审美。开发者让AI修复一个问题时，还可能发现另一个原本正常的功能突然失效。
这些问题解释了为什么多数团队都在强调流程。
有人给AI增加长期记忆，希望它理解项目此前发生过什么。有人建立版本管理，确保系统出现问题后还能回退。还有团队坚持让人完成最后验收，不允许AI自行宣布工作结束。
过去的AI游戏比赛更容易把注意力放在生成结果上。到了这场总决赛，选手开始思考如何管理AI，怎样让它稳定完成一项长期任务，以及人在整个过程中应该保留哪些权力。
这些看起来不如一张精美图片直观，却决定了AI能否离开演示现场，进入真正的生产环境。
当制作能力普及，洞察开始变得更贵
在大赛末尾的颁奖部分，“星光漫界”团队的《星光漫界智创平台》、ZNL团队的《Psych-MAP》获智能体赛道一等奖；游戏赛道一等奖为Anchor团队的《锚点》；《Autism is POWER》获动画赛道一等奖。
游戏赛道的16个项目来自完全不同的方向，不少参赛者也没有传统计算机教育背景。
他们学习人工智能，学习工业设计，或者长期关注教育和公益。过去，这些人很难独立完成一款游戏。AI让他们能够跨过代码与美术的第一道门槛，把对某个社会问题的观察迅速变成可体验的产品。
这种变化给游戏带来了新的可能。
当开发成本足够低，一款游戏未必要以传统玩家为唯一目标。它可以成为课堂上的教学工具，也可以帮助人们理解某类疾病。它甚至可以被用来规划一次旅行，或者改善一座村庄的适老化设计。
游戏在这些项目中仍然重要。它提供了互动方式，也让抽象知识获得即时反馈。但最终走到用户面前的产品，可能已经很难被传统品类所定义。
当然，创作门槛降低之后，竞争也会变得更加激烈。
当每个人都可以快速生成代码，单纯掌握工具很快就会失去优势。开发者需要更早发现未被满足的需求，也要知道哪些环节值得交给AI。更重要的是，他们必须愿意在原型完成后继续处理那些琐碎的工程问题。
从这个角度看，腾讯云把总决赛命题从游戏推向工作台，恰好触及了AI创作正在发生的变化。
一款游戏可以展示创意，一套稳定的工作流才能持续创造价值。决定项目上限的因素，也开始从谁更熟练地操作工具，转向谁更理解用户。
至少在这次路演现场，一批年轻创作者已经开始适应这种变化。
他们先用AI把游戏做出来，再把开发过程重新拆开，试着将成功经验留给下一个人。作品或许还显得稚嫩，但一种新的游戏生产方式，已经在这些工作台里露出了轮廓。 返回搜狐，查看更多

title: A love letter to the Guitar Hero X-Plorer Controller
text:
I peaked at 16 years old. I was part way through an expert run of 'Through the Fire and the Flames' by Dragonforce on Guitar Hero 3 at a friend's house for their birthday, and I remember thinking to myself, 'I don't think I'll ever top this'. As the song came to an end and I revelled in my passing grade, I got at least one nod of approval from the group before they slunk off to do what actually cool 16-year-olds do when presented with a free house and no adults around: smoke a big joint.
I've given it my all, on that same 20-year-old X-Plorer, with one of my favourite songs from that time.
Scroll down for my cool video.
Not me, though. I got high on sweet riffs, adeptly played out across five colourful buttons, slapped in near-perfect rhythm alongside a singular strum bar. Learn a real guitar? No, thanks. I'd rather sink 100s of hours into a rough approximation of the real thing—a karaoke version wrought of thin plastic from scaled-down body to hollow head unit. Plugged not into an amp, but an Xbox 360, with a whammy bar modulating not the strings, but the signal.
I played that momentous day on a legendary piece of kit: the RedOctane X-Plorer Controller for Guitar Hero.
The X-Plorer is about to celebrate its 20th anniversary. It came bundled with Guitar Hero 2, and I was 15 when it first came out here in the UK. That was in 2007. I'm 34 now. And that exact same X-Plorer controller from my proudest moment all those years ago?
It still bloody works. I use it all the time.
It's still in good shape. Its once white hue has yellowed over the years, and there's a little grime between the frets and the gaps in the plastic shell. But it's good. More than that, it's great . It even has the same Gibson sticker beneath the fretboard that I stuck on there as a teenager. There was another one, a bird of some sort? But it fell off. I'd forgotten where the stickers came from, but after searching eBay listings for the X-Plorer for this article, I realised they came in the box with it.
(Image credit: Jacob Ridley) I have a bit of a collection of guitar controllers on the go: two X-Plorers, two for Guitar Hero Live, and one CRKD Gibson Les Paul Blueberry Burst Pro Edition . That last one only came out last year, and yes, it's pretty sweet. I also have a Rock Band kit in an attic somewhere.
Yet the original X-Plorer from my childhood is still my favourite guitar controller of the lot. They all work on PC, with some small tweaks, but no other guitar has the smooth fret button actuation this one does. My fingers glide across those buttons, man. It just feels right.
The controllers I've had to tinker with the most are actually the Guitar Hero Live guitars. They're much newer than the X-Plorer, coming out in 2015, but that has seen the X-Plorer's ancient simplicity and stoicism replaced by modern proprietary- ness . Special remapping software is required to get the Xbox One wireless dongle working and to emulate the guitar in Windows (RB4InstrumentMapper with VJoy). The 20-year-old X-Plorer is simply plug and play.
(Image credit: Jacob Ridley) I also had to solder the battery cables back into place on one of the two GHLive guitars. That was my own fault. I left a set of AA batteries in one of them for maybe a decade. The batteries had, of course, exploded into a pool of corrosive battery acid, which subsequently chewed through the solder on the wires connecting the battery bay to the mainboard. That was a simple solder job, to be fair, it only took a couple of screws to pry the back off and expose the surprisingly empty innards, solder the cable, and put it back together. It works great now.
And, yeah, I actually kinda like the 6-fret layout from GHLive. It's a different challenge. It was like learning from scratch all over again when it first came out, and even 10 years on, I still basically suck at it.
Jacob Ridley Jacob Ridley The X-Plorer has only ever had one issue in twenty years: the whammy bar broke many years ago. It sort of just hangs limp from the guitar, modulating songs to a horrible pitch decided at random. I took it apart a few years ago and found the cause to be just a small piece of plastic that had broken off. This tiny plastic lip is what allowed the whammy to reset to its centre. It's an easy replacement for someone with a 3D printer. I don't have one right now (ex-housemate stole it—long story) so I've done something everyone recommends that's nearly just as good.
(Image credit: Jacob Ridley) I've wrapped the whammy bar in an elastic band, attaching on the other end to the guitar strap thingymabob. Now the whammy bar works perfectly. Simple things require simple fixes.
The other X-Plorer I own comes from when my partner used to work at a UK games retailer unimaginatively called GAME. Our local brand had just received a bunch of trade-in kit from someone clearing out their attic of old tat, and they'd dropped in a full Rock Band kit and X-Plorer controller, among other things. I happened to pop around that day as I worked in a shop nearby, saw the guitar behind the counter, and snapped it up pronto. I vaguely remember it cost just £2, but I can't say for sure. Whatever the price, it was a steal. They cost upwards of £50 nowadays.
I'm not opposed to newer guitars. The CRKD Gibson Les Paul Blueberry Burst Pro Edition is my go-to when I play YARG or Clone Hero. The Hall effect haptic strum bar is something else and it has an incredible number of programmable buttons. Moreover, it's wireless. I can lounge on the sofa while playing my sweet tunes.
(Image credit: Jacob Ridley) You can bet that I pre-ordered the new CRKD 8K Gibson Explorer Guitar Controller when that was announced back at Gamescom. I've never preordered anything faster in my entire life. I'm not normally one to pre-order anything, to be honest, but it's a brand new explorer. A brand new explorer . I've never been more the target audience for a thing.
Stage Tour looks sweet, too; although, I'm more than happy with YARG and Clone Hero. It was our frequent contributor and drumming apprentice Hope Corrigan that got me onto YARG. They use it for learning to play the actual drums . I've been playing throwback hits on guitar controllers ever since. Shout out to the people that make that game and Clone Hero. Both available for free and totally open to all. You are the true Legends of Rock.
(Image credit: Jacob Ridley) Look, I can go on and on about my many years of slapping colour-coded buttons in rhythmic order. Truth is, though, it's not just about the controller, or even the games. I've got so many good memories with these things. I started playing as basically a child, in my room, with my mate, Bob, who insisted on only ever playing with a controller. Bob is still a complete lunatic to this day. Or going to my first massive gig in Earl's Court in London and watching people play Guitar Hero on stage (I could've totally beat them). Or the many nights tapping along to My Chemical Romance, Paramore, Guns N' Roses, Black Sabbath, Rage Against the Machine with my friend James as we drank too many Relentless energy drinks, shredding the solo in Free Bird into the night.
So, in honour of the X-plorer's upcoming 20th anniversary, I wanted to do something special. I've given it my all, on that same 20-year-old X-Plorer, with one of my favourite songs from that time.
Please enjoy.

title: Embark should've implemented a PvE mode into Arc Raiders a long time ago
text:
I am very excited at the prospect of an Arc Raiders PvE-only mode. I have been ever since I got a tiny taste of what it could be like in Shared Watch , and even before that while playing in friendly lobbies. I know some aren't happy at the prospect of a mode with no PvP, but the only thing I can't believe is that Embark hasn't made this change sooner.
I've always thought that Arc Raiders was at its best in its early stages when players had to work together to take down high-value arcs. This kind of cooperation led to some genuinely hilarious scenarios or just nice encounters with strangers; something I hadn't experienced in an online multiplayer game for quite some time.
(Image credit: Embark Studios) At one point I remember being huddled in a bunker with another trio while trying to take down a Rocketeer on Spaceport. While we did manage to kill it, we were then caught out when a second Rocketeer turned up and we had almost no ammo left. It was a slightly bizarre situation to be found in with strangers. But it led to some very impressive strategy and coordination, and certainly a memorable experience, as we broke off into duos and ran in opposite directions, taking it in turns to distract the Rocketeer so we could all make a successful break for the extraction point.
I think this novelty is what brought a lot of players into Arc Raiders; it's certainly what kept me around for so long even after I'd completed expeditions and all the quests. But as more people left the number of fun encounters dropped and soon most of my interactions in Arc Raiders were just with liars, assholes, or cheaters. And that's not a great way to spend your free time.
If there had been a PvE mode this is when I would've transferred over to that. I probably would have even played Arc Raiders relatively frequently in said mode from there on, as I'm sure others who enjoy the simplicity of fun social interactions and taking down arcs would have as well. But with no other option than increasingly sour PvP lobbies I decided to retire my raider for the time being.
(Image credit: Embark) That's not to say PvP is absolutely no fun. Again, early on I had an absolute blast playing in trio PvP lobbies. The tension and strategic play was fantastic and felt really unique to Arc Raiders' ecosystem. Having to be cautious of both arcs and fellow players made games more hectic but that meant there was a better payoff when you all managed to extract in one piece with some hefty loot.
The weird and funny social moments that Arc Raiders did so well isn't exclusive to PvE or PvP lobbies.
It could also lead to equally hilarious scenarios. I still remember when my trio spotted another team from a mile off in Dam Battlegrounds who were clearly trying to flank us and just acting really suspicious. The only problem was they had absolutely no cover but also didn't seem to realise that if they could see us it meant we could also see them. Their surprise attack was quickly felled and then we had to explain to them how line of sight worked as we guided them to extract so they could go home to Speranza.
The weird and funny social moments that Arc Raiders did so well isn't exclusive to PvE or PvP lobbies. But PvE offers a guarantee that PvP can't: your games won't get ruined by assholes who lie or extract camp. And with no sign of the huge anticheat overhaul PvP would need to get fixed I can't see things changing anytime soon, so with that in mind I'd prefer something rather than nothing, because the world of Arc Raiders is simply too cool to watch waste away.
(Image credit: Embark) Embark has even admitted that a large chunk of Arc Raiders playerbase is PvE orientated , so I'd hardly be surprised if fair chunk of players came back just out of curiosity about what PvE lobbies could look like.
Unfortunately, there's no guarantee that this PvE test will even lead to a permanent addition. But I'll still be checking in to get a taste of what it could be like because a low-intensity Arc Raiders interlude sounds like great fun right about now.

title: The writer of The Witcher 3's best quest has returned to CD Projekt after a decade away
text:
That the quest 'Family Matters' stands out as the best quest in The Witcher 3 —a game filled with great storytelling and characters—is a true testament to the skill of its creators. That's why it's so exciting that one of the main forces behind it, writer Karolina Stachyra, has returned to CD Projekt after a decade away.
Stachyra's LinkedIn profile indicates that she's been working with the studio as a freelance consultant since February, and returned as a full-time writer in August. The quiet comeback went unnoticed until the weekend, though, when b0ysbrokenheart posted about it on X .
And here's the good stuff:
(Image credit: Karolina Stachyra (LinkedIn)) CD Projekt confirmed that Stachyra is indeed back in the fold, but declined to comment on what she's currently working on.
WHY ARE PEOPLE EXCITED?
We laid it out in 2015: What appears to be a simple missing persons job for Geralt slowly, painfully unwinds into "The Witcher 3’s most emotional and disturbing quest," driven by the conflicted, compelling, and deeply tragic character of the Bloody Baron. As we put it back when all this was new:
"It takes very real, important subjects—alcoholism and domestic abuse—and deals with them in a brutal, heartbreaking, and honest way. But, thanks to the blood-curdling botchling, it still feels like part of The Witcher’s dark fantasy world. It’s superbly written, brilliantly acted, and the branching paths make it well worth replaying. It’s The Witcher 3 and developer CD Projekt RED at their absolute best, and was the highlight of the game for many players."
As the writer of the dialog and cutscenes in Family Matters, not to mention her work elsewhere in the game and on the Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions, Stachyra's return to CD Projekt—following turns as narrative director at Techland and GSC Game World—is great news for RPG fans, regardless of what game she's working on.
(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) And since we're left to speculate on that, consider this: Ciri, the lead of the upcoming The Witcher 4 , was a central character in the Family Matters quest and key to demonstrating the depth and nuance of the Bloody Baron, who treated her like a surrogate daughter. Might an adoptive family reunion be in the works? It's not the worst idea I've ever heard.

title: I have broken GTA 5 by installing so many mods that the game only launches in windowed mode now
text:
Los Santos Customs
I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .
Can a game go on life support? Can it begin, in its dotage, to show signs of the ailment that everyone knows—but would never say—is the thing that will one day bring it down for good?
Grand Theft Auto 5 can. Installing my latest mod, Dynamic Traffic Colours , has brought my installation of the game to the point that it's failing death rolls. It will only launch in windowed mode, now. Trying to fullscreen the game before it has loaded will leave you suspended in the void. Quite literally: you will reside in an eternal black screen from which escape is impossible, unless you hold CTRL+ALT+DEL.
Anyway, once I was in and windowed, I encountered a mystery. The point of Dynamic Traffic Colours is to mix up the hues of Los Santos' cars. I think it is doing that, but with a conservatism that borders on timidity.
For the most part, the cars I see (and, to be fair, many of them more-or-less implode on spawn) are the same humdrum colours you get all the time. But then, like a vision, you get a car that's a garish mix of tints, sailing past you and into the side of a building.
This was literally the only one I could snap before it exploded or I teleported. Help. (Image credit: Rockstar) So I don't really know what's going on there. Perhaps it's a lesson to change my thinking. Rather than letting me gorge myself on clown cars, the mod presents them like rare, nourishing treats: oases in the windowed desert. I'm thankful for that.

title: Steam's tidying game trend is about to get the haunted meat it's been missing
text:
What happened:
I Am Your Beast and Clickolding developer Strange Scaffold has announced Something is Wrong with the Library , a tidying game set in "a library haunted by blood and meat."
Players will both reshelve the library's scattered books with a real Dewey Decimal System implementation while facing the accursed energies emanating from the corpses its billionaire patron entombed in the walls .
A "Modular Chaos System" ensures each playthrough has its own set of books to reorganize.
There's at least one terrifying, inscrutable obelisk.
Something is Wrong with the Library is set to launch before the end of 2026.
It's nice to see some aura in the tidying space
In recent months, Steam has been awash in organize-em-ups and haystack searchers —games capitalizing on the simple pleasure of arranging a chaotic melange into an orderly assemblage. But while I'd never think to deny the meditative appeal of putting a thing in a place, I'm not going to pretend that the emergent craze isn't undergoing the same gold rush of low-effort iteration that we saw during the rash of retail sims. Visit the page for the "Organizing" tag , and you'll find as many generic variations on "Tidy up the [X]" with AI logos as the Unity and Unreal asset stores can sustain.
With Strange Scaffold at the helm, however, I feel safe betting that Something is Wrong with the Library's haunted meat labyrinth will be able to offer a sense of identity and direction that's been hard to find among the available tidying sims. After all, this is a developer that was able to use clicking as a medium for a harrowing test of psychosexual fortitude . And then made a match-three metroidvania-slash-survival-sim-parody set in a weirdo dinosaur mansion. And then an isekai-enabling driving sim .
If nothing else, we can trust the studio to commit to the bit. It seems incapable—possibly pathologically—of doing otherwise.

title: CD Projekt lays out why you should play The Witcher 3 Remastered
text:
The Witcher 3 Remastered is coming out on September 29, which is tomorrow. That doesn't leave you a lot of time to make up your mind about whether you want to jump back in. So I, with a certain amount of assistance from CD Projekt Red, am here to help.
To begin, we must answer a question:
HAVE YOU PLAYED THE WITCHER 3: WILD HUNT?
If you answered no, and you have any appreciation for RPGs at all, then your situation just got a whole lot easier because, resoundingly, yes. Yes, you do want to jump in . With that out of the way, I will refer you to our guide to Witcher 3 Remastered release times around the world , so you can get on it.
If you answered yes, on the other hand, it gets a bit more complicated. We've already covered the lighting that had us like, 'Damn,' and wetter Tub Geralt , surely a compelling argument in favor. But if it's details you're after, here's the lowdown on what CD Projekt says are "the most important changes" coming to the new game.
Actually, before we get to that, we've also now got full and detailed system specs for a range of systems—CD Projekt revealed the new minimum spec earlier this year , but this new listing goes all the way up to the very high end. Note one change from the previously announced minimum: 60GB of SSD drive space is required instead of the previously indicated 70GB, but you'll need 95GB if you get The Witcher 3 Remastered on the Epic Games Store. (I don't know why, sorry.)
(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) As far as the rest of the rundown on "important changes," there's a lot going on here and it's not just a visual glow-up. A handful o' highlights:
Skills
Skills are now organized into a skill tree and each skill has three ranks. Unlocking new skills now requires having the necessary prerequisite skills rather than spending a set number of skill points.
Monsters
Polished the combat behavior of many non-boss monsters, including their attack patterns, counterattacks, movement, reactions, flight and the application of effects.
Moves
New idle and finisher animations, and improved ledge climbing, ladder climbing and vaulting animations for more responsive, fluid movement.
Views
Added new exploration and dynamic combat cameras, to make it easier to see what's going on no matter what's going on.
Of particular note are the new Accessibility options, including the new "Bard's Ballad" preset that aims to "reduce cognitive load for players who experience mental fatigue or have difficulty concentrating" by streamlining or disabling certain mechanics and features "for a smoother, more focused adventure."
I think this is a great idea: I generally like The Witcher's fussy systems (don't forget to brew your potions before a big fight!) but I can also easily understand why some people would want to just get to the good stuff without having to futz around.
Also note, for veteran Witcher-players who are still on the fence, that all of this is free for existing owners—consider yourselves nudged in the direction of do it .
Anyway, finally, here it is: Every change in The Witcher 3 Remastered that CD Projekt felt was important enough to write down.
Visual and Rendering
Implemented an improved shading model.
Updated multiple textures and models based on assets from The Witcher 3 HD Reworked Project .
Improved lighting and shading for grass and foliage.
Updated the visual effects of Signs, including their upgrade versions.
Added new visual effects for skills.
The game now features native DirectX 12 rendering with multithreading for better performance and visuals.
Updated tone mapping for improved colors, lighting, contrast and detail.
Added GTAO (Ground Truth Ambient Occlusion) as a new Screen Space Ambient Occlusion option.
Added Ray-Traced Local Shadows.
Updated Screen Space Reflections.
Updated Screen Space Shadows.
Updated the HDR calibration panel by adding new options and other improvements.
Improved Motion Blur with a higher-quality, more cinematic look.
Updated Subsurface Scattering for more natural skin rendering.
Improved terrain and material rendering for more natural lighting, shadows, reflections, and highlights.
Implemented new Image-Based Lighting (IBL) for improved ambient lighting and reflections across different environments.
Reworked Bloom for more improved lighting effects across different environments.
Gameplay
Improved the skill system. Skills are now organized into a skill tree and each skill has three ranks. Unlocking new skills now requires having the necessary prerequisite skills rather than spending a set number of skill points. IMPORTANT: As a result of these changes, your skill points have been reset.
Rebalanced the skill tree by refining skill bonus values, effects and synergies.
Renamed some skills to better reflect their effects.
You can now Reforge your equipment to change its appearance without affecting its stats. Only master craftsmen (Yoana and Hattori) offer this service. Unlock appearances by adding new equipment and crafting diagrams to your inventory. Dyes from Blood and Wine applied to equipment will carry over to the reforged item.
Polished the combat behavior of many non-boss monsters, including their attack patterns, counterattacks, movement, reactions, flight and the application of effects.
Added a new "Horse control input sensitivity" slider in Settings → Controls.
Improved Roach's and Geralt's movement, player control and animations:
Refined Geralt's jumping animation so that it feels more natural and polished. Note: This doesn't affect jump distance and height.
Added new finisher animations for Geralt.
Added new idle animations for Geralt.

Improved Geralt's gap closing animations in combat for smoother gameplay.

Added a new dynamic combat camera to increase visibility when fighting enemies.
Improved target-lock switching when moving the camera in combat.
Updated collision avoidance when riding Roach.
Polished animations for mounting and dismounting Roach, as well as cantering and galloping.
UI/UX
Meditation now features a timelapse instead of a UI screen for a more immersive feel.
The skill screen is now reorganized into a more intuitive skill tree layout.
Updated the map screen to make switching between tracked quests easier. Untracked quests now have a distinct marker and can be tracked by selecting it.
Increased the number of maximum markers on the map.
Added new map markers.
You can now hide herbs, boats and corpses on the minimap in Settings → Video → Interface for a cleaner, less distracting view.
Improved quest notifications by combining quest updates into a single HUD notification.
Nearby loot can now be grouped into a single window, so you no longer need to browse through multiple loot windows. You can enable this feature in Settings → Gameplay.
Added a loot feed that displays recently collected items on the left side of the screen. You can disable it in Settings → Gameplay.
Added item tooltips to the loot window, allowing you to preview an item's details before picking it up.
Renamed the "HUD Configuration" section in Settings to "Interface".
Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.
Photo Mode
Updated the Photo Mode UI and vastly expanded its features and options:
You can now choose from multiple different characters to place in your shot.
Added a selection of poses and expressions for Geralt and placeable characters.
Added a confirmation prompt before exiting Photo Mode to help prevent accidental exits.
You can now lock the camera position in Photo Mode to make sure you capture the perfect shot.
Added the option to apply different environment presets to your scene.
Added the option to save camera presets, allowing you to save and reuse camera positions and angles.
You can now change the aspect ratio of your screenshot.
Added the option to toggle a first-person camera mode so you can see the world through Geralt's eyes.
You can now enable or disable camera collisions with objects and walls.
Set the perfect scene by changing the weather and time of day.
Adjust the intensity of weather effects like rain or storms.
Added an option to toggle Rule of Thirds lines in various aspect ratios, with optional cinematic black bars.
Camera coordinates will now be visible in the UI.
Added an option to hide surrounding NPCs.
Added placeable props, giving you even more ways to create the perfect scene. Just don't ask where they all came from.
The cursor is now visible in Photo Mode on PC when using a mouse.
Accessibility
Added a new Accessibility section to the Settings menu. Moved existing accessibility-related options there.
Added the Bard's Ballad preset. You can enable it when starting a new game on the Just the Story difficulty or during the game in the Accessibility section. It is designed to reduce cognitive load for players who experience mental fatigue or have difficulty concentrating. It streamlines gameplay by simplifying certain mechanics and disabling select features for a smoother, more focused adventure. You can enable the preset in the Accessibility tab and customize it by enabling or disabling the following options:
Vitality Regeneration Boost - Gives the possibility to adjust its activation threshold ("Activates below (%) Vitality") and the rate at which Vitality increases ("Regeneration Intensity").
Infinite Breath - Geralt can't run out of oxygen while swimming and diving.

Streamlined tutorials to keep them concise and focused on teaching core game mechanics. We think Vesemir would approve.

Added Cross Platform Mod Support, an in-game tool powered by mod.io that allows you to easily browse and install player-created mods to customize your game. You can find it in the game's main menu in Mods. Log in with your CD PROJEKT RED Account, connect it to mod.io and start browsing. You can find more information about the Mod Manager here .

title: A 'fundamental' update for this 34-year-old survival game is coming in October
text:
Survival game UnReal World is getting an update this October: Here's why that's rad:
The game launched in 1992 and it's still getting patches
The 34-year-old game is considered the first open world survival game —it even has a Guinness World Record for it
Its creator, Sami Maaranen, has no plans to stop updating it : "When I accomplish one feature, I always have two more waiting"
The update will bring " fundamental new clothcrafting features " to UnReal World
This isn't just some simple outfits being added: " the most complex garments [take] days and days to craft "
That last bullet is important. Materials for garments are expensive: one of the screenshots in the patch notes shows a woman, Heta, bartering for nine feet of linen cloth with another characher. She is offering up a hunting bow, 5 arrows, and a handaxe, and the seller still isn't willing to close the deal.
(Image credit: Enormous Elk) "Heta is haggling over the price of 9 feet of linen cloth. That's just the length required for making an undershirt," the developer says . "Oh how light, soft and cosy undershirt it would make, but there is really a price to pay for that."
Yeah, this isn't a survival game where you quickly grab some plant fiber or animal skins and sprint to a crafting bench to instantly bang yourself out new set of pantaloons. It's gonna cost a lot and take quite a bit of time to make your clothing.
"I've already become quite fond of having the characters spend their evenings or short winter days crafting a whole new set of things, developing their clothcrafting skills, and enjoying the satisfaction of making good-quality garments for themselves," the dev says.
This is my favorite quote from the patch notes:
"Heta has spent several moonlit evenings making socks for herself. Few more evenings to go, and she can finally try them on."
Several evenings. Just making socks! And after a few more nights of hard work she'll be able to actually put them on. Now that's a survival game.
Here's UnReal World on Steam and the full announcement about " The Survivor's New Clothes" update . One more link: why not check out our 2025 feature about the two developers behind UnReal World , Sam Maaranen and Erkka Lehmus of Enormous Elk.

title: The internet is ritualistically murdering Discord's cartoon mascot
text:
Last week, Discord finally pulled the trigger on the global rollout of its age estimation systems, which require users to provide age verification through an ID scan or selfie if the company's estimation model can't confidently surmise that you're older than 18. While Discord estimated that 90% of users wouldn't need to prove their age, accompanying bugginess drove the company to address the emerging issues by posting on X with the air of being just a little guy.
Nobody liked that. Discord's ill-advised smol bean-posting has become a flashpoint for the internet's collective frustration over being forced to swallow what's widely perceived— with good reason —as the prelude to an inevitable exposure of private information. To vent that simmering resentment, X users have turned to creative outlets. By which I mean they've been drawing Wumpus, Discord's mascot, meeting a variety of grisly ends.
when you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs https://t.co/I9dVu9ZhET pic.twitter.com/BLAz9fWTSn September 24, 2026
While I don't recommend you browse the full selection of ritualized Wumpus-slayings—some of them are pretty gnarly—here's a survey of how the internet is processing its feelings about age verification.
Wumpus gets the Daguza Mackle treatment , by @Cassius_comm .
Saturn Devours His Chat Application, by @Ph4nt0m3nby .
Wumpus encounters the cruelties of fluid dynamics, by @Lizardbrainiak .
And, in emulation of that moment from the 2014 Godzilla that made me say "Jesus, Godzilla, who taught you that," there's this work from X user @Atlanticaph0tic :
(Image credit: X user @Atlanticaph0tic) There are more, of course: There are illustrations of Wumpus being drawn and quartered in historically brutal fashion, and .gifs of Wumpus being squished in a space pod by a legendary super saiyan before being exploded—both of which have been amassed a combined 400,000 likes and 8 million views.
I'm not an expert, but when the masses are cheering for your company mascot's cruel unmaking, I suspect there's been a PR misstep somewhere along the way.

title: World of Warcraft: Forever players find black market NPC who sells a 15-day movement speed buff and other rare items that nobody can afford yet
text:
Even though World of Warcraft: Forever is only in beta right now, players are able to explore a good amount of Azeroth to see what secrets Blizzard has tucked away for the full release.
Several secrets have been found, like a bunch of hidden books that reward powerful leveling items, but some of them have hints for what to expect when it launches in November. There are plenty of items that don't have a clear use yet that might become extremely valuable as time goes on.
A new NPC was recently found in the new Riverglades zone who sells a bunch of expensive crafting items. Theoretically, you should be able to get these items by playing the game normally, but many WoW: Forever players suspect he exists to prevent the auction house prices from skyrocketing due to their rarity.
Mister Graphed, the black market goblin merchant , sells items for 20+ gold—a hefty chunk of change in the Classic-era of WoW—that should prevent anyone from feeling obligated to buy them for more than that from other players. I'm sure it'll still happen because people love to sell items you can buy from vendors at a premium for the convenience of not having to travel around, but it will at least keep the prices from getting too ridiculous.
Notably, though, the vendor also sells new crafting materials called Fel Crystal and Stranglevine. Blizzard has done a big overhaul of professions in WoW: Forever, making them considerably more useful while you're leveling up. I was able to craft a nice set of gear before I was anywhere close to the beta's level cap of 20. These new items suggest there will be some really rare items to craft that never existed in previous versions of the MMO.
One item is available that isn't a crafting item at all: It's called the Gift of Galloping and it's a whopping 150 gold. This item says it gives you a 10% boost to your mounted movement speed for 15 days. Classic WoW never had anything like it, but I guess if you're rich you can pay a pricey subscription fee to go a little faster if you want.
It seems Blizzard is doing its best to prepare for WoW: Forever being a game that won't transition into new expansions. The level cap will permanently stay at 60, so there will have to be reasons for players to keep playing their characters or start new ones. It also means the economy will need things like that NPC in place so that the prices don't get out of control as players presumably get more powerful and the mysteries of the game get solved.

title: Double Fine's first game since being dumped by Xbox will be out in just 2 weeks
text:
It's been less than three months since Xbox kicked Double Fine Productions to the curb as part of the great "streamlining" that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is so excited to see . And just two weeks from today, the studio will release the first game of its post-Xbox existence: It's not what I expected, but it is most definitely a Double Fine game.
Thank You Bus Driver is a driving sim, but not of the sort you'd find in the Bus Simulator series. There are three—and only three—priorities:
Get To Your Next Stop , no matter what it takes
Keep the Schedule , because happy riders say thank you
No Breaking the Rules , and if anyone gets out of line, you give 'em a smack
Over on Bluesky, Double Fine described Thank You Bus Driver as "Crazy Taxi meets Papers, Please!" which sounds like exactly the sort of game the studio would make—this is, after all, the studio that gave us a multiplayer brawling game about pottery .
Clock in, drive the bus, and get passengers to their stops...but SLAP anyone breaking the rules (or throw 'em out the back if they don't behave)! It's Crazy Taxi meets Papers, Please! Launching October 14~Wishlist THANK YOU BUS DRIVER:doublefine.com/games/thank-you-bus-driver#buynow
— @doublefine.com ( @doublefine.com.bsky.social ) 2026-09-28T22:00:28.589Z Thank You Bus Driver doesn't look like a 'big' game, even by Double Fine standards (which I say with the utmost respect), and you may notice that it's being published by something called Double Fine Action Labs. In an interview with GamesBeat earlier this month, Double Fine CEO Tim Schafer said it's a label the studio will use for "experiments," such as the games that come out of the studio's Amnesia Fortnight game jams.
"They're complete games. They're not incomplete. But they're rough and scrappy and small. They're meant to be cheap and played for shorter amounts of time," Schafer said. Using the separate label, he continued, sets expectations at an appropriate level: "This is not Psychonauts 3. This is an experimental thing. We had a lot of fun with it, and we thought it was fun enough to share with people."
To be clear, Thank You Bus Driver is not part of the ongoing Amnesia Fortnite 2026, which will wrap up its very successful Kickstarter (and name a final winner) later this week. And it will be out very soon—on October 14, to be exact. You can wishlist it now on Steam , GOG , and Itch.io .

title: Former Elder Scrolls writer Kurt Kuhlmann is '100% convinced' a load-bearing bit of series lore was inspired by a typo
text:
Speaking on the FRVR Podcast last week, former Bethesda writer and designer Kurt Kuhlmann was asked about the concept of " Dragon Breaks "—time getting all weird on account of magic and stuff⁠—in Elder Scrolls lore. The biggest Dragon Break as far as Elder Scrolls fans are concerned: "The Warp in the West," the series' post-facto determination that every ending of The Elder Scrolls Chapter 2: Daggerfall happened at the same time. On account of magic and stuff, you see.
I love this story: Simple serendipity, a workplace oopsie, accidentally setting in motion the continuity and story beats of a billion-dollar franchise. Kirkbride is memetically famous among Elder Scrolls fans as a boundary-pushing loremaster who added a lot of weird flavor to Morrowind, so his affinity for the timey-wimey, fucky-wucky potential of the Dragon Break absolutely scans.
As far as I can tell, it doesn't seem like the series timeline Kuhlmann mentioned was ever publicly available⁠—this must have been an internal lore bible sort of thing. While TES Arena and Daggerfall designer Ted Peterson would write the in-game book, " The Warp in the West ," for Oblivion, Kirkbride and Kuhlmann appear to have introduced the concept in Morrowind with the books " Where Were You When the Dragon Broke " and " Dragon Break Re-Examined " respectively.
Kuhlmann noted in the podcast that he attempted to introduce more grounded, historiographic ambiguity with his treatment: What if the confusion was a matter of bias, transcription, and record-keeping, rather than metaphysical forces? Of course, Dragon Break Re-Examined also deliberately references events in Morrowind's future as the past, implying the skeptical book itself is yet another example of timey-wimey shenanigans⁠. An all-timer bit, for my money.
Elder Scrolls aside, the problem of preserving and representing RPG choice across multiple games in a series is something no studio has managed to fully "solve," if such a thing is even possible. I've always appreciated Bethesda's "fuck it, we ball" approach to the continuity with stuff like The Warp in the West. See also how Larian's Divinity: Original Sin 2 almost completely contradicts the story of Divinity 2: Ego Draconis (sans Original Sin) from eight years prior. I love RPGs so much, man.

title: I can't stop comparing the dialogue from the original, messy FF7 localization and its vastly improved fan translation
text:
"Final Fantasy 7 PC" is not an immediately intuitive combination of numbers and letters. Am I talking about the old trapezoid box version released in 1998? Or the "remaster" re-released in 2013? Or the first in the trilogy of remakes released nearly a decade later? Calling the 1998 version the "original" just makes things more confusing, since it isn't exactly the same as the PlayStation game released the year before.
When Square Enix updated Final Fantasy 7 to modern platforms in 2013 it had the chance to create something like the definitive version of the game, but instead it took some shortcuts, "improving" a few things from the original—like some of the notoriously rushed translation's grammatical mistakes—but more or less leaving the rest untouched. It's a worst of both worlds combination, where funny lines like "this guy are sick" get corrected to "this guy is sick" but the script as a whole remains confusing and frequently misrepresented in English.
Two years ago, fans released a monumental mod called the Shinra Archaeology Cut aimed at doing the script justice with a complete, top-to-bottom retranslation. It's one of a heap of FF7 mods available in the fan launcher 7th Heaven , alongside graphics overhauls, rebalances, a fan dub, and on and on. What I just learned today, though (courtesy of this ResetEra thread ) is that there's a meticulously maintained spreadsheet comparing every line of dialogue from the official PC release, the Japanese original, and fan translator TurquoiseHammer's new text.
Side-by-side, it's easy to see where the original English translation cut corners, misunderstood what was happening in the original text, or went too far in adding attitude that wasn't originally there. Sometimes that can be a smart choice when it comes to localization—"accuracy" isn't the be all, end all—but as you can see in a couple of the examples below, the official English script seemingly went edgy for edgy's sake.
While I think much of FF7's charm is tied to its messy translation, it's amazing to see a version of its script that isn't bafflingly vague and convoluted in key scenes related to Sephiroth and Cloud's identity. And instead of the official release's worst of both worlds pairing of fixed grammar but untouched everything else, the Shinra Archaeology Cut offers the opposite—an improved retranslation, but with an optional "Cultural Heritage Mode" that "restores a few memorably strange lines and infamous typos from the original English script." This guy are sick, now and forever.

title: This mod delivers what Valheim was missing all these years: seasons
text:
What's new
I've updated our best Valheim mods list just a week after publishing it.
Mostly because I'm sick and can't leave mods alone once I start, but also because I'm obsessed with turning the Meadows into a winter wonderland.
My latest addition is the Seasons mod (via Hexium ) by Shudnal .
The mod adds spring, summer, fall, and winter changes to Valheim's biomes.
It's customizable, so you can adjust season length, weather types, and more.
And now enjoy this clip of seasonal changes with the unholy sound of Valheim's deer bleating at 2x speed.
Valheim mod list update: Seasons
Valheim's 1.0 update isn't even a month old yet, but the modding scene is already filled with tons of impressive fan-made creations for custom worlds. My immediate favorites were quality-of-life mods fixing some of vanilla Valheim's most grating nuisances, but I've slowly tinkered with the more expansive stuff, like the aptly named Seasons mod by Shudnal.
Seasons does exactly what the name implies, adding four distinct and dynamic times of the year to all of Valheim's typically static biomes. Take the Meadows, for instance. Spring is lush green (as usual) before the summer heat slowly turns some patches of grass yellow. Then there's fall, which brings more orangey hues to the zone and darker evenings before transitioning into winter—snow-covered treetops and all.
And man, for someone who hates snow so much in real life, I love winter in a survival game. It feels like building a scene for a Christmas card, especially in a game as pretty as Valheim, but it's just not possible in vanilla until you're in the mid or endgame. Even then, I don't like building in the rocky terrain of the Mountains, and the Deep North is pretty, but hazardous. The Gammeltrolls don't give a damn about how hard I worked on my cabin. They're shotgun-blasting it with trees, and probably hitting me again with what remains.
More on the Seasons mod and its features
The chance to build in the snow-covered Meadows was my big draw, but there's way more to Seasons worth mentioning:
Biome events balanced around each season's weather
Seasonal lighting changes (Summer has the brightest nights, winter has the darkest, etc)
Traders change their wares over time to account for seasonal resource scarcity
Seasons impact player stats (Extra fire resistance in winter, more stamina in summer)
Configurable seasonal settings through add-ons like the BepInEx Configuration Manager

title: How to unlock transmog in The Witcher 3 Remastered
text:
Key deets
⚔️ You can transmog armor with Yoana at Crow's Perch after the Master Armorers quest.
⚔️ You can transmog swords with Hattori in Novigrad after the Of Swords and Dumplings quest.
⚔️ Any armor or sword Geralt picks up unlocks as a skin.
⚔️ It costs 100-200 coin every time you swap skins.
One of the big changes in The Witcher 3 Remastered is that you can now transmog armor and swords, swapping their skins at will.
You can't transmog at every blacksmith, only the two master smiths in the game, Yoana at Crow's Perch, and Éibhear Hattori in Novigrad, who will let you reskin armor and swords, respectively.
First, though, you have to complete their quests:
Master Armorers
Speak to Fergus Graem, the dwarf armorer at Crow's Perch, and ask about mastercrafted armor. Then Yoana will ask you to travel to Undvik in Skellige to recover some blacksmith tools.
Of Swords and Dumplings
Speak to Éibhear Hattori at his shop in Novigrad, northwest of Glory Gate, to start his quest and unlock him as a blacksmith.
Once you've unlocked Yoana and Hattori, simply choose the "reforge" tab on the top right when purchasing or crafting with them.
You can find Yoana in Crow's Perch castle CD Projekt And Hattori northwest of Glory Gate in Novigrad CD Projekt Each transmog will cost you coin CD Projekt A couple more quick things about transmog:
Transmog armor dyes the same colour as the base armor.
You unlock new sword and armor skins when you place them in Geralt's inventory.
Need a refresher on where to find witcher school gear?
🦅 Griffin : A medium set for signs
🐈‍⬛ Feline : A light set for glass cannons
🐻 Ursine : A heavy set for high defence
🐺 Wolven : A medium all-rounder set
Unfortunately this doesn't seem to be retrospective, so for endgame saves, unless you've kept every armour piece, you'll have to acquire them again, or at least take them out of your stash and place them in your inventory to unlock them—not the best system I'll admit, hopefully this will be patched.
Despite being a smith who forges grandmaster witcher gear, for some reason Lazare Lafargue in the Blood and Wine DLC can't transmog armor either. Again, fingers crossed this gets patched in.

title: How to get the Feline armor in The Witcher 3
text:
Key deets
⚔️ The Feline armor diagrams are in Novigrad.
⚔️ It has a level 17 requirement.
⚔️ You'll have to fight drowners, wraiths, a golem, and a witcher to get them.
⚔️ The upgrade diagram locations come from buying Adalbert Kermith's maps at the Blackbough merchant, Crow's Perch quartermaster, and Lindenvale's armorer.
The Feline armor is a light set of witcher gear that turns you into a bit of glass cannon. It has less damage resistance, but it buffs attack power, and provides a passive where strong attacks buff fast attack damage, and you can "backstab" enemies, with rear attacks hitting harder and stunning opponents. The set has four armor pieces, two swords, and a crossbow.
You can get the Feline armor in a cave on the north side of Temple Isle (the northernmost island) in Novigrad . You'll also need Keira Metz's Eye of Nehaleni from her questline to dispel the illusory rock blocking the entrance. I show the route in the video above, but otherwise:
On the map, head to the northwesternmost house on Temple Isle and follow the path you can see snaking around it, down the trail into the cave.
Fight the golem inside now or later and then take a left through the tunnel to the room with the statues in a circle.
Pull the lever beside each as many times as necessary to make them all face inwards—this will open a pool in the centre with drowners.
The key you need is on a corpse at the bottom of the pool. I recommend saving first, and then diving as fast as you can to grab it, sticking close to the wall to limit the drowners hitting you.
Head back to the main room and use the key to unlock the door behind the golem.
Defeat Mad Kiyan, the crazed witcher in the room, and loot the armor diagrams from his corpse.
Forge the Feline set at Crow's Perch, Novigrad, or Kaer Trolde's armorers, though remember that it has a level 17 requirement.
Read the laboratory log, also on Kiyan's body, and you'll get a marker for the location of the Feline Crossbow, which is in the Novigrad region as well.
Feline Crossbow
In the wreck of the Flying Stag ship on an island off the coast of west Novigrad, west of Drahim Castle and Lucian's Windmill.
Read Professor Sigismund Glogger's notes, also in the chest with the crossbow diagram to get the locations of the Feline Steel Sword and the Feline Silver Sword, again, both in the Novigrad region.
Feline Steel Sword
In Drahim Castle's basement just to the south of Novigrad's Glory Gate. Prepare to fight some bandits at the entrance.
Feline Silver Sword
In Est Tayiar to the northeast of Oxenfurt, east of the Vegelbud Residence. Destroy the wall to your right as you enter the ruin with Aard to find the diagram.
Once you've crafted the basic armor, you can upgrade it to enhanced, superior, and mastercrafted by finding the relevant diagrams.
Enhanced : Buy the Adalbert Kermith's first and second map from Blackbough's merchant to the west of Crow's Perch.
Superior : Buy Adalbert Kermith's third map from the Crow's Perch quartermaster.
Mastercrafted : Buy Adalbert Kermith's fourth map from Lindenvale's armorer, east of Crow's Nest.
Need a refresher on where to find witcher school gear?
🦅 Griffin : A medium set for signs
🐻 Ursine : A heavy set for high defence
🐺 Wolven : A medium all-rounder set
For grandmaster, when you head to Toussaint in the Blood and Wine DLC, speak to Lazare Lafargue in his armor shop in south Beauclair to start the 'Master Master Master Master!' quest to find the diagrams.

title: How to get the Wolven armor in The Witcher 3
text:
Key deets
⚔️ The Wolven armor diagrams are in Kaer Mohern.
⚔️ It has a level 14 requirement.
⚔️ You'll have to fight a lot of wraiths to get it.
⚔️ The upgrade diagram locations come from buying the notes from Éibhear Hattori in Novigrad, Lindenvale's armorer, Kaer Trolde's armorer, and the Hierarch Square armorer.
The Wolven armor is a medium set of witcher gear that functions as a bit of an all-rounder, buffing sign intensity attack power, and adrenaline point gain. It also has a passive that increases sword damage against bleeding enemies. It has four armor pieces, two swords, and no crossbow, similar to the Griffin set .
You can get the Wolven armor diagrams at the old signal tower just south of Kaer Mohern keep itself. There's a little puzzle involved in finding these, which I show in the video above, but otherwise:
Head inside, climb the ladder, and loot the chest to read Hieronymous's note.
Climb back down and use Aard to activate the teleportation crystal on the right side of the opening in the far wall.
Go back to the entrance and climb through the broken wall to the right, jump on the scaffolding on the north side of the tower, and walk along it to find the second teleportation crystal on a ledge to your right.
Go back inside and place the teleportation crystal in the housing on the left side of the opening in the far wall—use Aard to activate it.
Jump through the now-stable portal to land in a cave with a corpse. Defeat the wraith that appears and then loot the armor diagrams from the body.
Forge it at Crow's Perch, Novigrad, or Kaer Trolde's armorers.
Read the notes written in a shaky hand, which are also on the body in the cave, to unlock the locations of the Wolven Silver Sword and the Wolven Steel Sword diagrams, also in the Kaer Mohern area:
Wolven Steel Sword
In the Bastion directly to the west of Kaer Mohern keep, on a body in one of the burnt shacks as you enter. Prepare to fight wraiths.
Wolven Silver Sword
In the Ruined Watchtower to the north of the keep, along the west side of the lake. The enhanced steel sword diagram is also here. Prepare to fight more wraiths.
Once you've crafted the basic armor, you can upgrade it to enhanced, superior, and mastercrafted by finding the relevant diagrams.
Enhanced : Buy the well-preserved notes (boots, armour, silver sword) from Éibhear Hattori once you complete the Of Swords and Dumplings quest. You can find his home northwest of Novigrad's Glory Gate. Then buy the slightly torn notes (gloves, trousers, steel sword) from Lindenvale's armorer to the east of Crow's Perch in Velen.
Superior : Buy the damp, moldy notes (armour, silver sword, steel sword) from Kaer Trolde's armorer in Skellige. Then buy the heavily faded notes (boots, gauntlets, trousers) from Hierarch Square's armorer in Novigrad.
Mastercrafted : Buy the worn out and faded notes (armour, silver sword, steel sword) from Éibhear Hattori and the notes on parchment (boots, gauntlets, trousers) from Kaer Trolde's blacksmith.

🦅 Griffin : A medium set for signs
🐈‍⬛ Feline : A light set for glass cannons
🐻 Ursine : A heavy set for high defence
For grandmaster, when you head to Toussaint in the Blood and Wine DLC, speak to Lazare Lafargue in his armor shop in south Beauclair to start the 'Master Master Master Master!' quest to find the diagrams.

title: How to get the Griffin armor in The Witcher 3
text:
Key deets
⚔️ The Griffin armor diagrams are in Velen.
⚔️ It has a level 11 requirement.
⚔️ You'll have to fight wraiths, endrega, an ekimmara, and a wyvern to get them.
⚔️ The upgrade diagram locations come from buying Edwin Greloff's maps at the Midcopse blacksmith, the Hierarch Square armorer, and Éibhear Hattori, once you complete Of Swords and Dumplings.
The Griffin armor is a medium witcher gear set mainly focused around buffing the power of your signs, but also turning your Yrden into an AoE that reduces the damage you take, and further increases sign intensity when you're in it. There are four armor pieces, two swords, but no crossbow.
The diagrams to forge the basic Griffin witcher armor are located in Dragonslayer's Grotto in east Velen , to the northwest of Downwarren. The video above shows the route through this ruin, but otherwise:
Head inside, fight the wraiths, take a left at the end of the corridor and use Aard to blow open the cracked wall on its left side.

After killing the vampire, grab the armor diagrams from the chest up the stairs on the platform above.

Read Witcher George's Journal, also in the chest, to get the location of the Griffin Silver Sword and the Griffin Steel Sword, both of which are also in the Velen region. Remember, there is no crossbow in this set.
Griffin Steel Sword
In Hindhold watchtower in north Velen, directly east of the Border Post. Be prepared to fight endrega workers and warriors.
Griffin Silver Sword
In Lornruk lighthouse in west Velen, north of Heatherton. There's a wyvern nesting and you'll have to enter underwater via a cave with drowners.

Superior : Buy Edwin Greloff's third map from Hierarch Square's armorer in the center of Novigrad.
Mastercrafted : Buy Edwin Greloff's fourth map from Éibhear Hattori once you complete Of Swords and Dumplings. His home is northwest of Novigrad's Glory Gate.

title: How to get the Ursine armor in The Witcher 3
text:
Key deets
⚔️ The Ursine armor diagrams are in The Skellige Isles.
⚔️ It has a level 20 requirement.
⚔️ You'll have to fight sirens, wraiths, gargoyles, and a rabid rock troll to get them.
⚔️ Upgrade diagram locations come from buying Ibrahim Savi's maps from the Kaer Trolde armorer.
The Ursine armor is a fan favorite set in The Witcher 3, mainly due to its incredibly high damage resistance as the only heavy set of witcher gear available. It consists of four armor pieces, two swords, and a crossbow.
The diagrams to forge the basic Ursine witcher armor are located in northeast Skellige in the ruined castle on Urialla Isle , near the top of the Yngvar's Fang trail. I show the route in the video about, but otherwise, head to the Urialla Harbor fast travel and then:
Take the northeast path out of the village and go right at the fork until you hit the Trail to Yngvar's Fang fast travel.
Kill the rabid rock troll just ahead.
Follow the path along the cliffs and kill the sirens.
When you reach the collapsed section of the trail, slide down onto the broken stone walkway and jump across the gap to enter the fort via a wooden door.
Take a left down the spiral staircase, go to the end of the corridor, turn right, and pull the lever—this will open the cell doors and spawn some wraiths.
Drop down through the first cell to your left when facing back down the corridor.
Follow the path past where the next wraith spawns and climb through the broken hole in the wall into the throne room.
Forge it at Crow's Perch, Novigrad, or Kaer Trolde's armorers, though it has a level 20 requirement to equip
The chest containing the diagrams is just right of the throne, though be warned that taking these and pulling the lever to let yourself out will spawn three wraiths to fight.
Read the Chronicles of Clan Tuirseach, which is also in the diagram chest, to unlock the Ursine Crossbow and Ursine Silver Sword locations:
Ursine Crossbow
In the Siren's Cave on Svorlag in northwest Skellige, past the Old Watchtower in the south. Prepare to fight a lot of drowners.
Ursine Silver Sword
In the ruins of Fort Etnir in the north of the central island. Take the trail east and then north of Rogne. Prepare to fight two gargoyles.
Finally, read Knight Chalmir's Letter, from the corpse carrying the Ursine Silver Sword diagram, to get the location for the Ursine Steel Sword:
Ursine Steel Sword
In the basement of the ruined inn in the south of the central island. Head southeast from Fyresdal and prepare to fight sirens, plus wraiths in the inn basement.
Once you've crafted the basic armor, you can upgrade it to enhanced, superior, and mastercrafted by finding the relevant diagrams. You can get all of these locations if you buy Ibrahim Savi's first, second, third, and fourth map from the Kaer Trolde Armorer and follow the quest markers to acquire each upgrade diagram.

For the grandmaster upgrades, when you head to Toussaint in the Blood and Wine DLC, speak to Lazare Lafargue in his armor shop in south Beauclair to start the 'Master Master Master Master!' quest to find the diagrams.

title: This new super-bright 500 nit 'inkjet' tech promises to fix OLED's full-screen brightness limitation
text:
Ignoring the teensy tiny issue of burn-in , there's one remaining limitation afflicting large OLED displays including PC monitors. Yup, it's full-screen brightness. But now there's a new OLED panel tech that promises to fix that with a full-screen capability of fully 500 nits.
The new OLED panel is from Chinese manufacturer TCL CSOT and is derived from technology first developed by now-defunct Japanese OLED specialist JOLED. We've already seen the first PC monitor based on the TCL CSOT's novel inkjet-print OLED panel from MSI . But now a new generation of the inkjet-based tech has already been announced and it's much brighter than before.
This panel tech from TCL CSOT is known as "inkjet" because the OLED material is "printed" onto the display substrate using a process akin to inkjet printers. That's in contrast to the evaporation and metal-mask deposition techniques typically used by Samsung and LG in existing OLED panels.
Showcased by Vincent from YouTube channel HDTV Test at the IFA 2026 event , the demo panel is a 27-inch 4K model running at 120 Hz. The first-generation inkjet OLED panel from TCL CSOT in the MSI Pro Max topped out at 300 nits for full-screen brightness. That's roughly on par with the latest QD-OLED and WOLED panels from Samsung and LG, which are capable of 300 nits and 335 nits respectively.
Samsung and LG's panel's have been getting incrementally brighter with each generation, with both lines of OLEDs kicking off at 250 nits full-screen when they debuted in PC monitors a few years ago. But that process has been pretty long winded. At 500 nits full-screen, this new inkjet OLED therefore promises the single biggest leap in OLED full-screen brightness since the technology has been widely adopted for PC monitors.
Alienware's epic 5K2k 39-inch AW3926QW tops out at 300 nits. Imagine a 500-nit version... (Image credit: Future) For now, the wider specifications of the panel and exactly how this increased brightness is achieved isn't clear. We know the DCI-P3 coverage is 99% and, like the first-gen inkjet panel, this new technology offers true RGB-stripe subpixel structure, which bodes well for both clarity and colour brightness and vibrancy.
Speaking of colour coverage, one other detail that TCL CSOT has revealed is that inkjet OLED has another advantage in terms of colour volume. Apparently, both Samsung QD-OLED and LG WOLED have limitations maintaining full colour volume or coverage at lower brightness levels.
However, the new inkjet panel is claimed to maintain its colour volume regardless of brightness. The extent to which this is visible to the naked eye, I cannot comment.
Anywho, I've long taken the view that the problem of OLED panel full-screen brightness can be considered "solved" once it hits 500 nits. I can't see that in terms of full-screen brightness as opposed to small detail brightness, where currently available OLED monitors are already capable of 1,500 nits, anything much above 500 nits would be needed. Indeed, 500 nits full screen is well above what most people would find comfortable, day-to-day.
Yes, there will always be niche scenarios, perhaps involving strong ambient light and specialist displays for use outdoors, where well beyond 500 nits is needed. But for conventional PC monitor use cases, I think 500 nits has got to be enough to ensure a vibrant experience.
So, if TCL CSOT's claims are accurate and we soon see retail monitors with that capability, that will be game over in a good way for OLED monitors. Well, barring ye olde burn-in.
There's no word on when we might see this new panel tech in a monitor you can actually buy. Likewise, it's unclear what formats it may become available beyond the 27-inch 4K demo panel shown as IFA 2026. Watch this space.

title: How to get unlocked Multi Frame Gen working on an RTX 40-series graphics card
text:
Just in case you've been napping under a cool mossy rock since about January 2025, Multi Frame Generation (or MFG) is a frame rate boosting/game smoothing feature that leverages AI to create as many as five frames for every actually rendered frame. Nvidia introduced the original 2x Frame Generation feature with the RTX 40-series graphics cards in 2022. Sadly Nvidia restricted the more recent Multi Frame Generation version of the tech to RTX 50-series cards alone . Mmm, buttery; boo, proprietary.
But before you rush out to search in vain for an RTX 5090 at MSRP , it is possible to get most of the extra smoothness of MFG working on older Nvidia graphics cards—if you don't mind a little bit of software tinkering.
Before I tell you how, there's a few things to note. For one thing, Nvidia restricted higher rates of MFG to the RTX 50-series cards for a reason. At the risk of oversimplifying, the RTX 50-series' silicon is specifically designed to manage the extra frames in ways the older architecture is not. There's a dedicated AI Management Processor (AMP) which works alongside Flip Metering to get frames—rendered and generated—delivered to the display in as smooth a way as possible. The older architectures don't have these features dedicated to frame generation.
As such, CEO Jensen Huang has said in the past that bringing "the latest generation AI technology to the previous generation GPUs" is a good idea but that it would " require a fair amount of engineering ."
So it bears repeating the method for unlocking 4x MFG on a RTX 40-series card that I'm about to show you is definitely not officially supported. Besides that, one more thing to note is MFG is not a perfected technology—enabling higher levels of frame generation can introduce smeary frames and latency issues . Our Nick found that latency is an issue even with a frame rate limiter in place , too. Basically, all those extra frames may not actually offer the smoothest experience, depending on the game, even if the frame rate looks high.
But, if you'd still like to give it a go, here's how.
How to enable 4x MFG on RTX 40-series | In short
Download the ReShade HDR Installer .
Check the game you want to test supports MFG .
Select your chosen game from the left side panel in RHI.
Scroll down and click to install 'RTX 40 MFG,' and 'OptiScaler'.
Scroll back up to 'Nvidia Profile Overrides.'
Click on the blue button that says 'Multi Frame Generation'. Click 'OK' on the resulting dialog box.
In the box titled 'Multi Frame Generation', select 'Dynamic', 'Up to 4x,' and 'off' from the drop-down lists. Click 'Close'.
Launch your game. Select the relevant in-game Multi Frame Generation option.
How to enable 4x MFG on RTX 40-series | Breaking it down
(Image credit: RankFTW ) First things first, you'll need to download the ReShade HDR Installer (or RHI) from GitHub . This software automates the installation of unofficial mods like the post-processing injector referenced in the name.
When you open up RHI for the first time, it should import all of the games you already have installed. Before you do anything, make sure the game you want to test with your 40-series card actually supports MFG—Nvidia has a handy list of all the games that support DLSS Multi Frame Generation, and more of its snazzy RTX rendering tech right here . I'd recommend picking a single player game to test, as the mods you'll need to install can trigger in-game anti-cheat detection systems.
Once you've chosen the game you want to test, click on its name in the left side panel in RHI. You'll see a lot of game-specific options and mods come up on the main part of the RHI window. To unlock 3x and 4x MFG on a 40-series card, scroll down to the bottom of the list of options in RHI, then click to install 'RTX 40 MFG,' and 'OptiScaler'.
(Image credit: RankFTW ) Once those two unofficial mods are installed (this should only take a few seconds), scroll back up to 'Nvidia Profile Overrides.'
(Image credit: RankFTW ) Click on the blue button that says 'Multi Frame Generation'. A dialog box will pop up, saying 'Multi Frame Generation (MFG) and Dynamic MFG are only supported on Nvidia 50 Series GPU (Blackwell architecture)'.
(Image credit: RankFTW ) Click 'OK' on this dialog to open another box titled 'Multi Frame Generation'. This will feature three drop lists of options.
Under 'FG' I selected 'Dynamic', under 'Frame Count' I chose 'Up to 4x,' and I set 'Target Frame Rate' to 'Off.'
(Image credit: RankFTW ) If you're lucky, that's all the tinkering you'll need to do (if you're unlucky, you may need to swap between a few different driver versions within RHI). From there, you can launch your MFG-supporting game of choice, and then tweak the relevant in-game Frame Generation options.
Not all games offer a 4x MFG option specifically, so I sometimes relied on the FrameView app overlay to confirm it was active with my RTX 4070 Super. But otherwise, that's it!
Now go forth and enjoy some buttery smooth frame rates!

title: The Witcher 3 updated system requirements are in, and you will need an RTX 5080 for path tracing with DLSS and frame generation at 4K
text:
We all know that path tracing is a bit of a GPU hog, and if you plan on running it in the remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , you're going to need a beefy and relatively new rig for this graphical mode. However, to get the game up and running on the lowest settings at 30 fps, you won't need a very recent GPU.
With The Witcher 3 Remastered going live today, CD Projekt Red has shared what you can expect to run with every major CPU and GPU brand, with Low graphics at 30 fps requiring a relatively meagre Nvidia GeForce GTX 1660 / AMD Radeon RX 550 XT / Intel Arc A580 , plus an Intel Core i5 8400 or AMD Ryzen 5 2600.
However, for path tracing, you will need an Intel Core i9 13900K or AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D , paired with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 . To get the estimated 60 fps at 4K, you will have to not only run DLSS, but you will need to use frame generation. That does mean it should fare better at 1440p or 1080p. CD Projekt Red does not specify which level of upscaling (though it says it's on Auto, whatever that means) or what level of frame generation is present for this setting.
As we saw in our investigation of Pragmata's path tracing earlier this year, we are expecting The Witcher 3 Remastered's path tracing to offer better shadows and highlights to generally make the world feel more 'real'. However, whether or not it's worth the hit to performance will be dependent on your tastes (and your rig). I'm not personally sold on even ray tracing's benefits all of the time, so it would be a tough sell for me, even if I had a rig good enough to run it.

title: Thieves stole two Nvidia-emblazoned truck trailers in the hopes of getting hardware and instead got 40,000 lbs of sand
text:
If you assume any trailer with the Nvidia logo plastered on the side is loaded with electronics, you would be sorely mistaken. And if you're anything like the thieves who stole two trucks from self-driving truck software company PlusAI, you will be left with 40,000 lbs of sand instead.
As reported by Wired , an executive at PlusAI reportedly received a message from an acquaintance stating, “I have been proud of you for your adventure and success at PlusAI. Just saw two of your trucks near my work place! :)”
The problem here is that those two trucks were supposed to be outside a warehouse half a mile away.
It turns out that PlusAI has partnered with Nvidia (hence the Nvidia-emblazoned truck) to work on its autonomous vehicles, and these two trucks were part of a simulation. They were each filled with 20,000 lbs of sand. The trailers were forcibly detached from their vehicles, and thieves drove off with the cargo, only to dump it outside the acquaintance's office when they discovered the silica, instead of silicon, stashed inside.
If you were going to try and steal a truck trailer full of pricey equipment, it makes sense why anything with an Nvidia logo would be a potential target. The big green juggernaut became the world's first $5 trillion company late last year and has cashed in majorly on the AI boom.
Nvidia is continuing to make money hand over fist thanks to AI , and therefore one might expect that Nvidia-labelled trucks are filled with powerful GPUs or other such expensive equipment.
Still, this theft is probably a good sign to PlusAI that it needs to be very careful when it comes to monitoring stock, especially when it's got such a high-value company name slapped on the side of its trailers. If the sand simulation was a test to see if thieves would steal from its warehouse, I'd say its results have been well and truly achieved. I'd say the real reason was likely a bit more boring, though. Given it's a simulated load, that implies it was for weight-testing purposes.
All 40,000 lbs of sand have now been recovered by PlusAI, though the thieves have not yet been caught.
